name: Linagliptin
route_note: oral tablet 5 mg once daily; no dose adjustment for kidney impairment
tagline: A gliptin cleared mainly through bile, so one dose fits all levels of kidney function
summary: Linagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor used for type 2 diabetes that, unlike most gliptins, is eliminated mainly via the bile and gut, so it needs no dose adjustment in kidney disease. Large outcome trials (CARMELINA and CAROLINA) showed cardiovascular and renal safety.
mechanism: Linagliptin binds DPP-4 tightly and with high selectivity, preventing breakdown of the incretins GLP-1 and GIP. Raised incretin levels enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppress glucagon release, lowering blood glucose.
Its high-affinity, saturable binding to DPP-4 in plasma and tissues gives a long terminal half-life while the free drug is cleared mostly unchanged in faeces.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, monotherapy or combination

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: FDA approves Tradjenta in May 2011; the EU approves Trajenta in August 2011.

history.title: Boehringer–Lilly alliance
history.detail: Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly form a diabetes alliance to co-develop and co-market linagliptin, empagliflozin and other agents.

history.title: Glyxambi
history.detail: FDA approves the fixed combination of empagliflozin and linagliptin.

history.title: CARMELINA
history.detail: In patients with high cardiovascular and renal risk, linagliptin is non-inferior to placebo for cardiovascular outcomes.

history.title: CAROLINA
history.detail: Linagliptin is non-inferior to glimepiride for major cardiovascular events, with less hypoglycaemia.

pk.half_life: terminal >100 h; effective accumulation half-life about 12 h

facts: Linagliptin is the only widely used DPP-4 inhibitor that needs no dose adjustment for renal impairment.
It is developed and marketed through the Boehringer Ingelheim–Eli Lilly diabetes alliance formed in 2011.
